issues.description: The problem statement (and the provided solution) specify Stock.take(String) should return an int (returning -1 when the ingredient is missing or insufficient and a non-negative quantity otherwise). However, the template implementation of Stock.take(String) returns a boolean. This mismatch is structural and will prevent students from following the specification or using the solution's patterns (e.g., checking for -1) and can cause compile-time errors when implementing SealSaloon as described.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template's Stock.take(String) signature to return an int consistent with the problem statement and solution. Update its implementation to return -1 when the ingredient does not exist or quantity is insufficient, otherwise decrement the quantity and return the new quantity. This will align the template with the specification and the solution approach.

issues.description: The Stock.take method is represented with different return types across artifacts: the problem statement's UML defines Stock.take(String): int, the template implementation provides take(String) returning boolean, while the solution uses take(String) returning int. This mismatch makes it unclear which contract students should follow and can cause compile/runtime errors when following one artifact but using code or tests expecting the other.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the Stock.take signature across all artifacts. Recommended: change the template's Stock.take to return int (matching the problem UML and solution) and adjust its implementation to return -1 when the ingredient is missing or out of stock and the remaining quantity after successful decrement. Alternatively, if boolean is intended, update the problem statement UML and the solution to use boolean consistently and adapt usages accordingly.
